forecasts.reason: Cutting 1 epoch (238→213 steps) saves about 0.6 s at about 2 s/pp, so it loses about 0.4-0.6 pp from a margin that is already zero. The -0.5 point is not tested.
Saving about 16% of FLOPs gives about 0.5 s. Since CIFAR-100 is width-hungry, expect a loss above 0.25 pp.
The time cost is zero, but the weight-decay nudge sits inside the ±0.5 pp noise. Beating E016 by 0.2 pp (to 0.7627) is unlikely.
The time cut is about 5%, short of the 8% the hypothesis needs, and the depth loss is about 0.3 pp.
The 20 px phase lowers the pixel fraction by about 0.026 of V, saving about 0.2 s (about 3%, under 4%). Early steps are not free (E018).

cruxes: Is there any time-neutral accuracy lever worth at least 0.4 pp (BN-stat recompute at 32 px, EMA tuning, a wider group 1 run at low resolution)? Without one, every trim fails the 0.753 bar.
How large is the rebuild-only accuracy shift? If identical code ranges from 0.7537 to 0.7607, the keep decisions are noise-driven, and a 10-seed check of the tip is worth more than another trim.
Is the measured price of every trim really 1.5-2 s/pp, or is some lever (group-1 depth, middle-phase resolution) cheaper than 1 s/pp once noise is averaged out?
